newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk says output, exports on track.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk says output, exports on track.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals combine, part of RAO Norilsky Nikel, produced over 8,000 tonnes of nickel in August and plans slightly higher levels for September, a top company official said on Wednesday.

Mikhail Steklov, director of mining and metallurgical works at Norilsk's main non-ferrous metals complex in the far northern city of Norilsk, told Reuters by telephone that output was proceeding according to planned levels for 1996.
"We are fulfilling the company's plan for this year and have had no problems with production," he said, adding that a cut in gas supplies earlier this month had not hit production.
"There was no effect on output," he said, adding that September output would rise four percent on year-ago levels.

Alexei Parshikov, head of exports at Interros, a financial-industrial group that includes Norilsk and its shareholder Uneximbank and handles some of Norilsk's exports, said exports were going according to plan.
"The loading situation is being decided and things are going according to plan," he said. He declined to elaborate.
The Kommersant daily newspaper reported that an unidentified quantity of export nickel that tax authorities had been examining was being loaded onto a vessel on Tuesday.
A Russian nickel trader in Moscow said Norilsk had been late this week in loading material for export.

"They appear to have delays in loading (for export) some material -- in any case, we did not get what we were scheduled to receive today," he said. "We don't know when we will get our stuff -- maybe tomorrow."
Norilsk's top management, from Moscow, is in the Arctic town of Norilsk this week to negotiate wage arrears and other issues with workers at the Dudinka port who had threatened to strike.

Kommersant also said that the head of the Krasnoyarsk regional administration, whose jurisdiction includes Norilsk, had called for a temporary administration to oversee matters at the Norilsk combine.
Norilsk had said it expects overall output for 1996 at all its nickel units to rise three percent on 1995's 180,000 tonnes.
It sees its copper production up six percent on last year's 338,700 tonnes.
